summary: Execution-plane audit delivery key (cinatra#2266 slice 2, design gap G4) — ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS audit_events.execution_delivery_key text, then CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS audit_events_execution_delivery_key_key ON audit_events (execution_delivery_key). The column alone would be additive; the UNIQUE index on a table that exists on every deployment is what makes this a migration, per the convention's 'a unique index on an existing table counts here too'. It cannot fail on existing rows: the column is brand new so every historical row is NULL, and this is a PLAIN unique index (not NULLS NOT DISTINCT), so Postgres treats those NULLs as distinct and the constraint binds exactly one producer — the execution plane, the only writer that supplies the column. No dedup pass is needed because there is nothing to dedup. WHAT THE COLUMN IS: the broker's durable audit spool (packages/execution-plane/src/service/audit-spool.ts) stamps each record with a PHYSICAL delivery identity `<spoolId>:<recordId>` — spoolId persisted per single-writer volume, recordId a spool-local monotonic counter allocated at the pre-dispatch reservation and surviving a crash. Delivery is at-least-once by design (a broker that dies before its batch is acknowledged re-delivers the same keys) and this unique index is what makes that harmless: the second insert conflicts, logExecutionAuditEventDurable reports `duplicate` instead of minting a fresh randomUUID row, and one execution yields exactly one audit row. It is NOT the logical correlation key (jobId + seq + decision), which stays in metadata — see #2266 G2 for why a logical key cannot be the delivery key. The operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap shape in src/lib/drizzle-store.ts and the Drizzle table in src/lib/authz/audit-schema.ts, both updated in the SAME PR: a fresh install bootstraps the post-migration shape and ledger-fakes the chain, an existing deployment executes this module at boot / `cinatra db migrate`. Idempotent (both statements guarded); unqualified names ride the runner's search_path; stays in its own transaction rather than using CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, whose failure mode (a leftover INVALID index) is worse than a sub-second ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on an append-only audit table. A fail-loud postcondition asserts BOTH the column and the index exist in the current schema, so a partial or skipped apply RAISEs and rolls back rather than leaving a shape the idempotent insert would silently double-write against. down() drops the index then the column — lossless for every other producer (none ever wrote it) and costing exactly one property for the execution plane: a rollback re-exposes the window in which a re-delivered record writes a second row, which is the pre-#2266 behaviour a pre-#2266 image asks for. SEQ 0088 — strictly greater than the max seq on live origin/main (core__0087_drop-dashboards-visibility) and greater than every seq claimed by an open PR at authoring time; seq is assigned at MERGE, so a rename-only renumber of this module plus this fragment is normal if a concurrent lane lands first (the runner tolerates gaps). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
